people.name: Germano Silva Lopes
people.summary: Former Samarco manager of structural projects (projetos estruturantes). Convicted on 3 September 2026 by Brazil's TRF-6 federal appeal court, in a unanimous ruling, of causing a flood resulting in death and of environmental crimes over the 2015 Fundão dam collapse, which killed 19 people. Sentence: 8 years 9 months in prison, starting in the closed regime, plus 192 day-fines. Appeals are still open. The pages opened do not set out what this manager personally did.

posts.role: Manager of structural projects (Projetos Estruturantes); Diário do Grande ABC calls the post general manager (gerente-geral)

records.what: A substitute federal judge in Ponte Nova, Patrícia Alencar Teixeira de Carvalho, acquitted Samarco and this manager in a ruling signed on 14 November 2024. Reports differ on how many people that covered: A Gazeta says 21 executives and technicians; Diário do Grande ABC lists five people by name. Prosecutors and victims' families appealed.

On 3 September 2026 the TRF-6 Second Criminal Panel partly reversed the 2024 ruling. It convicted this manager, the two other managers and Samarco, and upheld the acquittals of the other defendants. Crimes: causing a flood resulting in death, plus environmental crimes. Sentence: 8 years 9 months in prison, initial closed regime, 192 day-fines of 1/30 of the minimum wage each.

people.disputed: Convicted on appeal, but the conviction is not final: further appeals are still open (Correio da Manhã; O Fator), and The Rio Times reported that none of the three goes to prison immediately, because Brazilian criminal appeals normally run their course before a sentence begins. No page opened up to 4 November 2026 reports an appeal filed. The law firm Maurício Campos & Brasileiro represents the three; it had not answered A Gazeta by publication, and no statement from them was found. Samarco says it "nunca teve conhecimento ou foi informada de risco de ruptura da barragem de Fundão" (it never knew of, and was never told of, a risk that the dam would fail). The first-instance judge had acquitted them in November 2024; A Gazeta gives the reason as lack of proof of individual acts. The pages opened do not set out what each manager personally did.

people.name: Chen Yuan-cheng
people.summary: Chairman of Formosa Ha Tinh Steel on 30 June 2016, in most reports; some say president. His name is also spelled Chen Yuan Cheng (陳源成), and Vietnamese papers write it Trần Nguyên Thành. A film clip of him apologising for the plant's discharge and the mass fish deaths was shown at the Vietnamese government's news conference that day. He is described only as speaking: no page opened shows him charged, or shows an act of his own in the discharge.

posts.role: Invited as vice chairman and chief executive (Taipei Times); named president (Kallanish)
posts.years: joined Formosa 1 August 2014 (Kallanish); Kallanish's report naming him president is dated 6 January, with no year shown on the page opened

posts.role: Chairman (most reports); President (Vietnam Government Portal, VTV, VOA photo caption)
posts.years: on 30 June 2016; start date not found

records.what: Formosa Plastics Group invited him, a former China Steel president, to serve as vice chairman and chief executive of the Vietnam steel company, while William Wong acted as chairman.

In a letter to staff on the morning of 30 June 2016, as chairman, he blamed subcontractors, citing the environment ministry's findings: "This is the results we don't want to hear, but we respect the investigation of the government."

In a film clip shown at the news conference on 30 June 2016 he said, as Viet Nam News reports it in English: "We take responsibility for the incident and deeply apologise to the people of Việt Nam, particularly the residents of Hà Tĩnh, Quảng Bình, Quảng Trị and Thừa Thiên – Huế provinces."
Formosa promised $500 million. Government office chief Mai Tien Dung suggested the admission might be enough to avert prosecution.

people.disputed: Not charged on the pages opened; the company admitted cause. Title: Viet Nam News, VietnamPlus, The Nation, Dan Tri, the Hanoi Times, AP, RFA and Taiwan's TechNews say chairman. The Vietnam Government Portal and VTV say president. The VOA page (Reuters) says president in its photo caption, and in its text quotes the "chairman of its steel unit" as Tran Nguyen Thanh. That is very likely the same man, not a second person: Trần Nguyên Thành is the Vietnamese reading of 陳源成, and Báo Pháp Luật gives that name to the chairman who wrote the same letter to staff. No page opened says so outright. Wording: TechNews says his statement was translated from Chinese into Vietnamese, so the English quotes are translations and differ. AP: "Our company takes full responsibility and sincerely apologizes to the Vietnamese people"; Vietnam Government Portal: "Our company accepts full responsibility for the incidents and would like to express our sincere apologies". His letter to staff put the fault on subcontractors. The Nation places the news conference on a Wednesday; AP and the Government Portal say Thursday, and VietnamPlus, the Hanoi Times and TechNews date it 30 June 2016, which was a Thursday. No page dates the filming of the clip.

people.name: Kapil Kumar C Saratkar
people.summary: Deputy inspector general of police, Tirunelveli Range, at the Thoothukudi police firing of 22-23 May 2018, in which 13 people were killed (Scroll; UNI). The Aruna Jagadeesan Commission named him among 17 police personnel for departmental action, "without prejudice to launching criminal action". A commission is not a court. It found that one shooting took place at his instance and a deputy superintendent's, and another by a gunman on his instructions, both without the inspector general's knowledge. The pages opened do not say whether anyone was killed in those two shootings. He has not been charged on any page opened. Tamil Nadu told the Madras High Court on 31 August 2026 that disciplinary action against him had been dropped.

posts.role: Inspector General and Commissioner of Police, Madurai City

records.what: The commission's report, placed before the Assembly on 18 October 2022, found: "Thus, there is a spectacle of the DIG, disregarding even the presence of the IG and arrogating to himself the authority to issue directions for shooting." It said a shooting at the instance of the DIG and DSP Lingathirumaran, and one by gunman Shankar on the DIG's instructions, were without the IG's knowledge. The article does not give the place or date of those shootings, or say whether anyone died in them.

The commission recommended action against him and 16 other police personnel for "acts of commission and omission departmentally without prejudice to launching criminal action". The South First, citing Frontline, reports that it named him among officials who "certainly exceeded the limit".

The government sought his explanation on 17 October 2022. A DGP letter of 11 November 2023 said no FIR (police case) had been registered against the police named in the report. The state's status report that month said the DGP was looking into the replies, and gave no details of what the senior officers said.
A Tamil Nadu government release of 2 January 2024 said departmental action had been taken against 17 police personnel, naming him. It did not say what the action was.

An affidavit by the Chief Secretary, put before the Madras High Court's Madurai Bench at the hearing on Monday 31 August 2026, said the disciplinary action against him had been dropped, along with that against the then IG and the then collector. The article gives no date for the affidavit itself, and no date or reason for the dropping.

Reported 11 September 2026: the state refused to reconsider the "previous DMK regime's decision to drop disciplinary action". The Advocate General said there was no statutory obligation to carry out the commission's recommendations in full.

Reported 29 September 2026: the court disposed of the public-interest petitions, holding that "no further orders can be issued", and refused to entertain a contempt plea against the CBI director while a protest petition is before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Madurai. The report records no finding by the court on him.

people.disputed: Named for action by a commission; a commission is not a court. Not charged and not convicted on any page opened up to 4 November 2026: The South First says the CBI named only one police officer as accused, Inspector Thirumalai, and petitioners' counsel and the state's counter-affidavit (The Hindu) say the same. The CBI is doing further investigation on a Madurai magistrate's order (The Hindu), and a protest petition is pending there (UNI). The state told the court, in the same undated counter-affidavit, that police fired only on the orders of an Executive Magistrate and that the CBI found no material to prosecute the officers. The state's accounts of action against him differ: proceedings initiated (The Hindu), "under examination" (The News Minute, December 2023), action "taken" (January 2024 release), and dropped (affidavit, August 2026). A petitioner claims the CBI gave the officers a clean chit, which led to the dropping (UNI). No statement from him was found; officers' replies were submitted between November 2022 and May 2023, and the government has not made them public (The News Minute). Deaths: Scroll and UNI say 13; The News Minute's own text says 14 while quoting the commission's 13. Spelling: Scroll's October 2022 story and part of SabrangIndia write Karatkar, and Deccan Herald writes C Kapil Kumar; each gives the same post and the same list of officers. The Indian Express links the Madurai City commissioner of 2026 to the DIG of 2018.
